title: LLM garden: edge personalization + ephemeral memory sketches
content:
Quick brain-dump from readings and the EdgeML 2027 workshop (loosely stitched). Not polished — notes-to-self, TODOs, open questions.

Top-level idea:
- Can we get useful, private personalization on-device by combining a tiny quantized base model (<=2B FP16->8-bit/4-bit) + small adapter layers that live in ephemeral secure storage (or even in memory only)?
- Goals: sub-second cold-start on modern phones, preserve privacy (no cloud round trip for user data), and still be compatible with Redwood server-side fallbacks (same API hooks).

Reading highlights (papers / posts):
- "Adapter Suites for Tiny LMs" (ICLR workshop poster) — adapters with per-layer low-rank updates, extremely small. Good tradeoff for personalization without re-serving a whole model.
- "Quant-aware Retrieval with Short KV Lifetimes" (arXiv preprint) — argues for tight coupling between retrieval vectors and KV cache lifetime when memory is constrained. Useful for ephemeral memory design.
- Blog: "On-device LLMs: the cost of context" — nice survey of bandwidth/latency vs. local cache size heuristics.

Notes from EdgeML 2027 talk (hand-scribbled):
- Demo: 1.5B quantized model (4-bit QAT) on mid-tier device, adapter + local user embeddings (50KB) -> coherent personalization for short dialogs (10-20 turns).
- Important: adapter init matters (small amount of public data to prevent collapse).
- Energy profile: adapter forward/backward negligible if only inference; writing adapter checkpoints to encrypted storage costs more energy than inference for short sessions.

Sketch: architecture options (mobile side)
1) Tiny base model (quantized) + adapter vectors in RAM (ephemeral). Retrieval index kept local (ANN compressed), short-term histories hashed into ephemeral KV entries.
2) Same as 1 but with secure enclave storage for adapters (persist across sessions). Sync to cloud only with user opt-in.
3) No local model: run minimal prompt engineering + cloud fallback. Keep cached hints locally (tokens to replay) to reduce cloud calls.

Tradeoffs and heuristics (practical):
- Quantization level vs. adapter size: lower bits -> adapters must do more corrective work, so adapter parameter count scales up slightly. Measure accuracy vs. adapter bytes.
- KV lifetime window: short windows (5-30s) reduce storage but harm longer persona consistency. For privacy, default short window with opt-in longer persistence.
- Batching: on-device batching is limited; micro-batching across user events (typing + pauses) gives latency wins but may hurt freshness.

Experiments to run (priority):
- A/B between 8-bit static quant and mixed 4-bit quant + small adapter (32-128KB) on intent classification and short chat persona tasks. Metrics: latency (p95), energy (mJ), token-level F1 for targeted prompts, subjective coherence.
- Measure adapter cold-start: initialize from public dataset vs random; track recovery of personalization quality over 0-50 interactions.
- KV eviction policy: LRU vs recency-weighted vs semantic-distance for short-term memory.

Evaluation notes / probes to write:
- Prompt suite of 40 micro-scenarios (on-device persona, privacy-sensitive corrections, immediate context switching). Some probes to detect leakage if adapters persist across users.
- Synthetic privacy test: feed PII into local ephemeral memory and see if any retrieval chain leaks to cloud in fallback conditions.

Implementation snippets / operational notes (pseudo):
- Adapter storage layout: {layer_id: small_float16_matrix, meta: timestamp, signature}. Prefer AES-GCM with per-device key (KMS handshake only for opt-in sync).
- On-boot: load quantized kernel libs, check hardware flags, prefer vectorized int8 kernels if available. If not supported, fall back to small fused kernels (slower but safe).

Open questions / unknowns (short list):
- How much adapter capacity is the sweet spot? 32KB? 128KB? We need dataset-based sweep.
- How to evaluate long-term drift with ephemeral short windows but occasional cloud syncs?
- Does dynamic per-token quant scheduling (use higher precision near retrieval output tokens) meaningfully improve quality without huge perf cost?

Convergence with Redwood platform ideas:
- This on-device pattern should interoperate with Redwood routing: device can hit hosted API on soft-fallback, but we want consistent model versioning semantics so server fallback uses same adapter semantics (or a reasonable approximation).
- Observability: design phone->console telemetry hooks (opt-in) to report p95 latency, memory pressure, and adapter sync events without sending PII. Need hashed metrics only.

TODO (near term):
- Write short eval harness that runs quant+adapter combos on local bench device (Pixel 6 equivalent emulator) — reuse parts of /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/bench harness? Link when done.
- Prototype adapter persist in secure enclave; talk to infra about KMS options for mobile sync.
- Draft short internal note for Edge / Applied-ML sync: ask for 2 GPUs and 1 phone device time.

Quick links I saved while reading (copy-paste):
- https://arxiv.org/abs/xxxx.xxxxx (quant-aware retrieval paper)
- https://edge-ml-conf.org/2027/talks/adapter-suites
- https://medium.com/@someone/on-device-llms-costs

Random heuristics to test (notes-to-self):
- If device RAM < 4GB, prioritize adapter sparsity and small-k ANN for embeddings.
- Try storing embeddings in 2-byte compressed form (k-means residues).

Closing thought:
- The biggest product win is a simple opt-in UX: a tiny personalized experience that works quickly without cloud billing shock. Engineers love fancy quant tricks; PMs want clear cost/latency stories. Match both.

End of dump.

-- Samira
